Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the MediCore Health Systems Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, please do not place your line on hold, as this may cause feedback into the conference. Today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss MediCore Health Systems' financial results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on the call are Michael Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Jennifer Hayes, Chief Financial Officer; Robert Kline, Chief Medical Officer; David Patel, Chief Operating Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Strategy Officer; and Mark Esposito, Chief Information Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that certain statements made during this call may contain forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks, uncertainties, and other factors that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Michael Reynolds.

Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on our performance for the third quarter. We continue to execute on our strategic priorities, focusing on delivering high-quality patient care, expanding our network, and improving operational efficiency.

Today, I will provide an overview of our key achievements during the quarter, focusing on seven key aspects: average reimbursement rates by payer category, capital expenditure guidance for the next quarter and year, capital expenditures for facility modernization and expansion, same-facility volume and revenue growth guidance for the next quarter and year, net patient revenue year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter, operating margin guidance for the next quarter and year, and revenue per admission trends and drivers.

These areas highlight our progress in navigating reimbursement pressures, investing for growth, and driving sustainable profitability. Now, I’ll turn the call over to Jennifer Hayes to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Jennifer Hayes:
Thank you, Michael. Good morning, everyone. As Michael mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Net revenue for the third quarter was $2.48 billion, an increase of 7.8% compared to the same period last year and up 2.1% sequentially from Q2. This growth was driven by increased patient volume, favorable payer mix, and the successful implementation of our revenue cycle management initiatives.

Our operating expenses were $2.05 billion, representing 82.7% of net revenue. We are continuing to focus on managing our costs effectively while investing in key growth initiatives, particularly in revenue cycle optimization and facility upgrades.

Net income for the quarter was $180 million, or $1.45 per share. We are pleased with our financial performance and remain confident in our ability to achieve our financial goals for the year.

To give everyone a deeper understanding, let me walk through these seven key aspects in more detail, starting with our average reimbursement rates by payer category, which was a major driver behind our revenue growth this quarter. In the hospitals and healthcare services space, payer mix and reimbursement dynamics are crucial for our top line, especially with ongoing pressures from CMS rate updates, commercial payer negotiations, and the shift toward value-based care.

Our consolidated average reimbursement rates as a percentage of gross charges—our payor yield—came in at 48.2% for Q3 2024, up 110 basis points year-over-year from 47.1% in Q3 2023. This is the third straight quarter of sequential improvement, thanks to a favorable payer mix shift, proactive contract renegotiations, and early successes from our revenue cycle management overhaul.

Breaking it down by major payer category, Medicare, which represented 52% of our net patient revenue—up from 49% last year due to aging demographics and Medicare Advantage penetration now at 38% of our Medicare lives—delivered an average reimbursement rate of 68.4% of gross charges. That's a modest 1.2% decline year-over-year, mainly from CMS's FY2024 IPPS update, which included a 2.7% lump-sum increase offset by a 0.5% productivity adjustment and documentation improvements related to the two-midnight rule clarifications. Our Medicare Advantage sub-segment held steady at 72.1%, benefiting from star ratings uplift—our average MA plan rating across partnerships with Humana, UnitedHealthcare, and Aetna hit 4.2 stars, unlocking bonus payments estimated at $15 million for the year.

Medicaid, at 18% of net patient revenue, saw our strongest performance with rates at 54.7% of gross—up 320 basis points year-over-year. This was fueled by state-directed payment programs in our core markets: Texas and Florida expansions under the 1115 waivers added $28 million in supplemental payments, while our Georgia facilities captured full upside from the state's new managed care carve-in for inpatient services. We faced some headwinds in California, where Medi-Cal rates lagged at 48%, so we optimized our service line mix there by de-emphasizing low-yield elective orthopedics.

Commercial payers, comprising 25% of net patient revenue—flat year-over-year despite some membership contraction—averaged 112.3% of Medicare benchmarks, or roughly 82.6% of gross charges. This was a solid 4.1% improvement, thanks to mid-year renegotiations with Blue Cross Blue Shield affiliates and Cigna, securing 3-5% rate bumps tied to quality metrics under shared savings arrangements. Our fee-for-service commercial yield hit 118% of Medicare, but managed care dragged it down to 105%, reflecting tighter utilization management from payers like UnitedHealthcare's OptumHealth division. Self-pay and other categories rounded out at 6% of net patient revenue with a 32.1% yield, bolstered by our enhanced charity care screening via the Epic MyChart patient portal, which reduced bad debt expense by 12%.

Regionally, there's meaningful variance underscoring our portfolio strategy. In the Southeast—our largest footprint with 45% of beds—yields averaged 51.2%, driven by high commercial density in Florida and payer-friendly dynamics post-Hurricane Ian recoveries. The Midwest, at 42.8%, faced pressure from Illinois Medicaid redeterminations, dropping 2.1% year-over-year, while our Northeast urban clusters like Philadelphia benefited from 6% commercial uplift via density-based contracting with Independence Blue Cross. Rural facilities, 15% of our system, continue to outperform at 46.5% yield, thanks to Critical Access Hospital designations and CAH cost report optimizations.

On trends, we're seeing a continued mix shift: Medicare Advantage now 20% of total lives, up from 16% two years ago, which compresses blended yields short-term but stabilizes cash flow with 95% capitation predictability. Value-based reimbursements now account for 28% of commercial revenue—double year-over-year—with our ACO REACH participation generating $42 million in shared savings, primarily from reduced readmissions via our post-acute partnerships with Encompass Health.

Strategically, we've invested $75 million in our RCM tech stack this year, rolling out Change Healthcare's Pareo platform alongside Epic's Contract Manager for real-time denial analytics—denial rates are down 18% to 7.2%. We're also piloting AI-driven coding with 3M 360 Encompass in 20 facilities, targeting a 2-3% yield lift from HCC recapture. Looking ahead, we expect FY2024 blended payor yield to hit 49.5%, with Q4 upside from commercial renewals and CMS's proposed 2.9% outpatient APFS bump. Risks remain around site-neutral payments—the Lower Costs, More Transparency Act could shave 1-2% off outpatient yields if passed—but our 60/40 inpatient-to-outpatient shift positions us well.

This reimbursement profile gives us strong visibility into our 5-7% EBITDA margin expansion guidance.

Next, on capital expenditure guidance for Q4 2024 and full-year fiscal 2025, this remains a critical lever in our long-term growth strategy amid the ongoing recovery in procedural volumes and structural tailwinds in the healthcare services sector.

For fiscal 2024, we've deployed approximately $520 million in capex through the first three quarters, in line with our initial guidance of $650 million to $700 million for the full year. This spend has been heavily weighted toward high-ROI investments supporting margin expansion goals, including the completion of three de novo ambulatory surgery centers in high-growth Sunbelt markets like Phoenix and Dallas-Fort Worth, and the rollout of next-gen Epic EHR modules across 65% of our 42 acute care hospitals.

For Q4 2024, we are guiding capex to $160 million to $180 million, representing about 25% of our full-year budget. This quarter will see acceleration in spend for key initiatives: facility expansions and capacity buildout at 45% of Q4 capex, or about $75 million, including OR expansions at flagship facilities in Atlanta and Orlando to capture the rebound in elective orthopedics and cardiology procedures, running 15% above pre-pandemic levels per our case mix index data—this includes adding four new hybrid ORs with Siemens Healthineers' Artis icono angiography systems, enhancing procedural efficiency by 20-25% through AI-enabled imaging.

Medical equipment refresh at 30%, or $50 million, focuses on upgrading diagnostic imaging with GE Healthcare's Precision DL PET/CT scanners at eight community hospitals in the Midwest, reducing scan times by up to 40% while improving radiologist throughput, critical amid CMS's 2025 OPPS cuts of 2.9% on imaging reimbursements.

Digital health and IT infrastructure at 20%, or $35 million, supports cybersecurity hardening post the Change Healthcare cyberattack, including Palo Alto Networks firewalls and zero-trust architecture, plus Phase 2 of our telehealth platform integration with Zoom for Healthcare, targeting a 30% increase in virtual inpatient consults to drive ancillary revenue.

Maintenance and other at 5%, or $10 million, covers routine HVAC upgrades for energy efficiency, aligning with ESG commitments to cut Scope 1 emissions by 15% by 2026.

Regionally, 60% of Q4 capex flows to our Sunbelt footprint—Texas, Florida, Arizona—where patient days grew 8% year-over-year in Q3, fueled by demographics and lower commercial denial rates versus the Northeast. Midwest and Pacific Northwest hospitals see lighter spend on equipment to stabilize occupancy amid Medicaid mix pressures.

For fiscal 2025, we're raising our capex outlook to $750 million to $800 million, a 15-20% increase over 2024, reflecting strong free cash flow generation—we expect $1.1 billion in FCF this year—and conviction in volume growth. This is a 4.5% capex-to-revenue ratio, in line with peers like HCA and Tenet, focused on outpatient shift.

Breakdown: facility expansions/ASCs $320-350 million or 42%, for 5 new ASCs and 10 hospital ORs targeting 12% EBITDA margins; medical equipment $220-240 million or 29%, robotic surgery with Intuitive Surgical da Vinci Xi at 15 sites and 4th-gen MRI fleet; IT/digital $150-170 million or 21%, AI diagnostics via Nuance Dragon Ambient eXperience and full Epic Willow ambulatory rollout; maintenance/sustainability $50-60 million or 8%, solar arrays at 10 facilities and supply chain resilience.

This positions us to outpace capacity constraints—with a 10-15% staffed beds shortfall per AHA—we'll add 250 incremental OR hours annually, capturing share from freestanding ERs and PE-backed ASCs. We're leaning into value-based care pilots with payers like UnitedHealthcare, where AI-driven length-of-stay predictions shave 0.5 days on ortho DRGs.

Upward pressure from 5% YoY construction inflation and equipment lead times is offset by JV structures—70% of expansions are 50/50 physician-hospital partnerships. Risks include labor shortages or CMS site-neutral policies, but our 95% on-time delivery track record gives confidence. Payback periods average 2.5-3 years, driving 200-300 basis points EBITDA margin expansion over 24 months.

Moving to capital expenditures for facility modernization and expansion in Q3, we deployed $285 million in total capex, up 18% year-over-year and aligning with full-year guidance of $1.1 billion to $1.2 billion—the highest quarterly spend in our history, part of a multi-year $4.5 billion program through 2027.

Modernization accounted for 62% or $177 million, expansion 38% or $108 million. These boost adjusted EBITDA margins by 150 basis points over 24 months through higher throughput, reduced length-of-stay, and improved CMI.

Facility modernization, with 3-4 year payback, accelerated upgrades: imaging overhauls with 12 new 3T MRIs and 8 dual-source CT scanners across Southeast and Midwest at $45 million, yielding 22% QoQ imaging volume increase to 85% utilization from 72%, capturing lucrative outpatient procedures in Sunbelt where MA exceeds 50%.

Surgical robotics and OR optimization at $38 million funded 15 da Vinci Xi systems, bringing fleet to 85, with 15% uplift in robotic procedures commanding 20-25% higher reimbursements, complemented by LeanTaaS software reducing turn times by 18 minutes, boosting OR EBITDA to 32%.

Digital health at $52 million for Epic MyChart and Nuance Dragon Ambient eXperience in 20 hospitals, reducing clinician documentation by 25%, addressing RN shortages—vacancy down to 8% from 14%—and Cerner/Oracle predictive analytics targeting 1.2 day ALOS reduction.

Sustainability at $22 million for HVAC retrofits and solar microgrids at 10 facilities, achieving LEED Silver, cutting energy 15% or $8 million annually, positioning for $500 million green bond in Q1.

Modernization skewed to urban Southeast 45%, Midwest 30%.

Expansion added 12% net beds: $65 million for 220 beds including Miami tower and Austin micro-hospital, ramping to 75% occupancy in 18 months via Optum bundled payments; $28 million for 8 ASC JVs with 90%+ margins, 28% same-facility growth; $15 million behavioral health in Phoenix.

We're exiting three low-performing rural hospitals to fund Sunbelt growth, where redeterminations add 5-7% volumes. Q4 capex $320 million, 65% modernization; financing 40% operating cash ($450 million Q3 FCF), 35% revolver, 25% bonds, net leverage 3.2x.

These transform us into a high-margin operator for MA expansion (35% revenues) and MIPS.

Now, on same-facility volume and revenue growth guidance for Q4 2024 and FY 2025: guiding 3.5-4.5% volume growth in Q4 on adjusted patient days, building on Q3's 4.1%, and 4.0-5.0% for FY2025, excluding recent ASC tuck-ins.

Inpatient 3-4% Q4, 4-5% FY25, from elective rebound 15% above pre-pandemic, CMI to 1.87, ALOS 4.5 days. Outpatient 5-6% Q4, 5.5-6.5% FY25, endoscopy/imaging up 8%, ED 4% via telestroke/tele-ICU at 80% penetration.

Sunbelt 5-6%, Florida 7%; Midwest/Northeast 2.5-3.5% amid 42% MA penetration.

Revenue growth 5.5-6.5% Q4, 6.0-7.0% FY25, plus 150-200bps RevPAR from 4.2% commercial, 2.9% IPPS, da Vinci across 70 facilities. MA denials 18%, but collections 97.5%.

Initiatives: $250 million high-acuity lines for 200bps volume, Genentech CAR-T 12% oncology; 35% VBC for $15 million savings; labor turnover 14%.

Risks: seasonality, MA cuts; upside: ASCs.

Next, net patient revenue totaled $2.48 billion in Q3, up 2.1% QoQ from $2.43 billion, 7.8% YoY from $2.30 billion—11th straight YoY growth from procedural rebound, payer management, outpatient shift.

QoQ: 3.5% patient days from 4.2% admissions to 58,200, elective ortho/cardio up 6%, ALOS 4.7 days via AI tool in 75% hospitals. Rev per day down 1.2% to $1,682 from MA, but appeals recovered $12 million. Outpatient $1.54 billion up 4.8%, 62% mix from 15 ASCs.

Southeast 65% growth, commercial 42%; Midwest softer but telehealth +22%.

YoY: inpatient +9.2% to $940 million, CMI +2.4% to 1.68 from Medtronic robotics in 28 hospitals. Outpatient +12.1% to 1.2 million encounters, rev per admission +4.6% to $42,600 from 4.2% commercial, 2.7% IPPS. Payer: commercial 42%, Medicare 38%, Medicaid 14%; bad debt 2.1%.

Hub-and-spoke model, 250,000 VBC lives, $45 million savings.

Q4 6-8% YoY growth.

On operating margin guidance: Q4 8.0-8.5%, FY24 7.9-8.1% up from prior, FY25 8.2-8.8% or 40-60bps improvement.

Volumes: elective +12%, Sunbelt CMI 1.82, commercial 52%, VBC 22% for 50bps from readmissions -15%.

Labor 52% costs, inflation 4.2%, productivity +2.5% via Cerner; 340B $60 million FY25, ortho implants -8%.

Southeast >10.5%; Epic $30 million efficiencies, AR 45 days.

Pillars: ASCs 15-20% margins, $1.2 billion M&A, biosimilars 3-4% drug savings.

Finally, revenue per admission reached $15,420, +8.6% YoY, +2.3% QoQ, outpacing peers, stacked +16.4%.

CMI 1.94 +3.7% from ortho/neuro 22%, da Vinci in 28 facilities, GLOS -4% ortho; cardiology +12% RPA to $28,500, DRG +2.8%.

Commercial 47% +320bps, Sunbelt 62%, MA 12% at 92% FFS, denial 3.2% via Waystar +$18 million.

Ancillary 42% growth: pharmacy $2,850 +11%, oncology CAR-T +14%; observation $4,200 +9%.

Southeast $16,100 +10.2%, Midwest $14,600 +6.8%, West $15,900.

Epic HCC +2.3% CMI, Cerner AR 42 days, 4.5% commercial uplift.

Future: $400 million transplants CMI 2.00, VBC bundles 65%, ancillaries +15%, M&A +300bps. Guide 7.5-9% FY RPA $15,800-16,100.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Robert Kline for an update on our clinical initiatives.

Robert Kline:
Thank you, Jennifer. Good morning. We are making significant progress in improving clinical outcomes and patient satisfaction. Our bundled payment program has shown promising results, with an 18% reduction in readmission rates. We are also focused on leveraging technology to enhance the patient experience and improve care coordination, specifically through our telehealth platform and remote patient monitoring programs, which have increased patient engagement by 25% this quarter.

Following that, David Patel will provide an update on operational efficiency.

David Patel:
Thank you, Robert. We are focused on streamlining our operations and improving efficiency across our network. We have implemented several initiatives, including lean management processes and centralized supply chain procurement, which have resulted in $45 million in cost savings and improved patient flow, reducing average length of stay by 0.3 days system-wide.

Next, Lisa Chen will discuss our strategic initiatives.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you, David. Our strategic priorities remain focused on expanding our network, developing new partnerships, and investing in innovative technologies. We are actively exploring opportunities to grow our footprint in key markets like the Sunbelt and enhance our service offerings through joint ventures with physician groups and payers for value-based care.

After that, Mark Esposito will discuss our IT infrastructure and cybersecurity.

Mark Esposito:
Thank you, Lisa. We are committed to maintaining a robust and secure IT infrastructure to support our operations and protect patient data. We have implemented several new security measures, including advanced firewalls and zero-trust architecture, to enhance our cybersecurity posture and ensure compliance with HIPAA and other regulatory requirements. Importantly, we experienced no material disruptions from recent industry-wide threats.

Now, I'd like to turn the call back to Michael Reynolds.

Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, everyone. At this time, we will open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Our first question comes from Alex Rivera with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Good morning. Can you discuss the impact of the recent cybersecurity threats on your operations and patient data?

Mark Esposito:
Good morning, Alex. We saw no direct impact to our operations or patient data from those threats. Our proactive investments in cybersecurity, including the Palo Alto firewalls and zero-trust model Jennifer mentioned, ensured full continuity. We've also enhanced monitoring to stay ahead of evolving risks.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen:
What are your plans for expanding your telehealth capabilities and remote patient monitoring programs?

Robert Kline:
Thanks, Emily. We're scaling telehealth to 100% facility coverage by year-end, integrating it deeply with Epic for seamless consults, targeting 30% growth in virtual visits. Remote monitoring is expanding via wearables in our post-acute partnerships, reducing readmissions further and adding ancillary revenue streams.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lopez with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

David Lopez:
Can you provide more details on your strategic partnerships and their potential impact on your business?

Lisa Chen:
Absolutely, David. Our JVs with ortho groups and payers like UnitedHealthcare for bundles are ramping, adding high-margin ASC capacity and shared savings. These could contribute 200 basis points to volume growth next year, strengthening our position in value-based care.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Kim with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

Sarah Kim:
Thanks. On capex, how are you prioritizing amid higher guidance?

Jennifer Hayes:
Sarah, we're prioritizing high-ROI areas like ASCs and robotics for quickest paybacks. Sunbelt focus captures demographics, financed prudently to maintain leverage.

Michael Reynolds:
Thank you for the questions. In closing, I want to thank our dedicated employees for their hard work and commitment to providing high-quality care to our patients. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value to our shareholders.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you for your participation in today's call. This concludes the MediCore Health Systems Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
